RA-1: A small flat stone sits on top of the cairn, set there by a stranger's hand. From here you can see the next cairn across the heath, and from that one the next. Raidho is a road held together by sight, one marker leading to the one after. Which cairn can you see from where you stand?
RA-2: A small flat stone sits on top of the nearest cairn, set there by someone's hand. From there you can see the next cairn across the heath, and from that one the next. Raidho is the road made this way, each step showing the one after. Standing beside this stone, where does your eye go first?
RA-3: A flat stone rests on top of the nearest cairn, set there by a hand you never met. From it the next cairn stands in view across the heath, and from that one, the one after. Raidho is a road that reveals itself one marker at a time. Which cairn is in sight from where you are now?
RB-1: On the nearest cairn, the top stone sits a little crooked, left by a hand before yours. From it you can see the next, and from that one the next, across the whole heath. Raidho is a road that shows itself one stretch at a time. What does the next cairn show that this one cannot?
RB-2: One flat stone sits wedged on top of the nearest cairn. From it you can see the next cairn across the heath, and from that one the next. Raidho is the road that runs this way, each marker handing you on to the one beyond. What does the next cairn let you see that this one cannot?
RB-3: A small flat stone caps the nearest cairn, set there to be seen from far off. From where you stand, the next cairn shows grey across the heath, and beyond it another. Raidho is the road that lets each mark lead the eye to the next. From this cairn, what does the next one show you?
ASK0-1: Plainly, then, Kuky. Isa is ice, a stillness that holds while everything around it moves on. The question asks what you are waiting to receive before you reach for the cup. It points at something that would have to come from outside first, a permission, a certainty, someone else moving, a better moment. I cannot tell you which one, or whether there is one at all. Isa only names the pause. It does not say whether the pause still protects something, or has simply outlasted what it was waiting for.
ASK0-2: Isa is the rune of ice: something held still while everything around it moves on, like the cup going cold. The question asks what that stillness is waiting for before it acts. It could be permission from someone, certainty that it will go well, a sign that the moment is right, or for the thing to feel worth wanting again. The rune does not say which, and neither can I. Isa names only the pause, and that what waits in it does not stay as it was.
ASK0-3: Isa is ice, Kuky, a halt that holds while everything around it keeps moving. The question asks what that halt is resting on. It could be permission from someone, or certainty that the choice is right. It could be a moment that feels better than this one. Isa does not say which, and I cannot see it from here. What the rune does hold is plain: the pause stays still, but what you pause over does not, as the cup cooled. Which of these it is, only you can name.
ASKN-1: I'll say it plainly, Kuky. Isa is ice, a stillness that holds while everything around it keeps moving. The question asks what that stillness might be waiting on. It could be permission, a word from someone else that this matter is yours to take up again. It could be certainty, some proof that the thing is still worth the effort before any effort is spent. Either may be so, or neither. Isa does not name what is waited for. It names only the waiting, and that what was set down has not moved since.
ASKN-2: Plainly, the question asks what has to come from outside before you return to something you set down yourself. Isa is a standstill. It keeps a thing as it was, while time moves on and takes the warmth from it. What you wait for may be permission, someone's word that it is still yours to pick up. It may be a reason, a sign that the moment has come, as if the right time were handed to you rather than chosen. Either may be so, or neither. Which fits is yours to say.
ASKN-3: Isa is ice, something held still while everything around it moves on. The question asks what you might be waiting to receive before you take up the thing you have set aside. It could be permission, someone else saying it is yours to take. It could be certainty, knowing the moment is right before you reach. Isa does not say which, and it does not call the waiting wrong. It names the holding, and the cooling that comes with it. Which of these fits, if either, is yours to say.
